brenor_heartsteel_10.m: That weapon...must you hold it where I can see it? Even in death I know its glow.

brenor_heartsteel_20.m: Wrong? To you it is a finely forged weapon. To us...it was an executioner's tool.

brenor_heartsteel_30.m: When the Shadow rose, many who came for the Elytharans carried heartsteel. It cut through armor with frightening ease, but that was never what we feared most.

brenor_heartsteel_40.m: Those struck down by heartsteel often found no peace. Too many never reached Elythara's embrace. Instead, they lingered...as you see us now.
r: So these weapons created the ghosts?

brenor_heartsteel_50.m: No. The weapon was only a tool. It was those who wielded it, and the darkness they served, that filled our halls with restless souls.
r: I never knew any of this.

brenor_heartsteel_60.m: I believe you. Had I thought otherwise, I would not have spoken with you. Keep your weapon if you must, but remember what it once meant to my people.

brenor_heartsteel_70.m: If you want to talk about something else, then please, get it out of my sight.

brenor_help_50.m: Speak the names of the lost when you can. We were men once, not shadows in stone. That is all a slave could hope for.
r: I will honor your memory by continuing my search.

brenor_intro_10.m: The pick is light in my hand and heavy in my memory. We were driven into the deep seams with only a lamp and a promise. Many never climbed back.
r: What was it like down there?

brenor_memory_40.m: Hardship was the only thing we owned. The mountain took the rest. But remembering us is enough. Few living souls do.
r: I will remember that, but I must continue my search.

brenor_refuse_10.m: I will not speak while that glowing stone is in your pack. It stirs old pain. Set it down and return if you want my words.
r: All right. I will set it down.

brenor_story_30.m: Dark, cold, and full of smoke. The tunnels shook when the rock groaned. We dug at glowing seams until our hands bled. The overseers said the ore was precious to Nor City, though none of us were told why. We were tools, nothing more.
r: Is there anything I can do to honor you?

brenor_who_20.m: My name was Brenor. I came from the lands ruled by Feygard, back when its people still followed Elythara. I was taken during the rise of Garthan I, when those who held to the Light were chained and sent below the mountain. I swung this pick as a slave until the stone claimed my breath.

undertell_book.10: I found the skeletal remains of an adventurer near the mining rails in Undertell. Among the remains were a history book titled "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History" and a necklace marked "Jewel of Fallhaven", which made me wonder if this man was from Fallhaven.
undertell_book.30: Ysrine suggested that the history of Undertell records what could be measured, but avoids the voices of those who suffered here.
undertell_book.40: I brought the book to Fallhaven. Arcir recognized it as a deliberate account of Undertell's past and asked me to return and listen for what the book omits.
undertell_book.50: In Undertell, I spoke with Brenor, an Elytharan ghost who still remembers himself and the weight of the mines.
undertell_book.60: I encountered an Elytharan cooker slave who spoke only of labor and routine, remembering work but not belief.
undertell_book.70: I earned the trust of a shy Elytharan ghost named Cora, who would only remain when I approached in silence.
undertell_book.80: The Elytharan ghosts each revealed a different truth: identity, labor and silence. I think Arcir would like to hear about this.
undertell_book.90: I returned to Arcir with what I learned about the Elytharan dead and the omissions in the history of Undertell.
